Universally fix a finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, equipped with its Borel measurable structure, a function V:E→ℝ, nonnegative-real parameters α,β, and a real η. The complete caller conditions are α>0 (after coercion to ℝ), α≤β, V is twice continuously differentiable, 0<η, βη≤1, and, for every x,v in E,
α||v||² ≤ ((D(DV)(x))(v))(v) ≤ β||v||².
Here the two derivative evaluations are exactly the iterated Frechet derivative quadratic expression, and E may have dimension zero.

Define μ as volume exponentially tilted by -V using the supplied normalized-tilt convention. Define J as the pushforward of μ×stdGaussian(E) by (x,z)↦(x,x+sqrt(η)z), ν as the second marginal of J, and Λ as the pushforward of J by (x,y)↦(y,2x-y). Independently define F(x,y)=(x,2x-y). Thus Λ uses a different ordered-coordinate map from F. Set mY to the pullback sigma algebra along the second coordinate. Work with the product measurable structure and its internally derived inclusion mY≤the product sigma algebra.

Write L=L²(J;ℝ), N=L²(ν;ℝ), and H=HP=lpMeas(ℝ,ℝ,mY,2,J), the closed subspace associated with second-coordinate measurability. Let i:H→L be its inclusion. Let CE:L→H be the displayed condExpL2 operator and define P=i∘CE:L→L. The displayed internally constructed measure-preserving map snd:(E×E,J)→(E,ν) supplies M:N→L, the linear isometric pullback u↦u∘snd in L² classes.

The proposition concludes that μ,J,ν are probability measures; H equals the range of P as a linear map; and P fixes every included f in H. It further concludes that there exists a Markov kernel S:E→Measure(E) such that, for EVERY y in E,
S(y)=volume.tilted[x↦-V((y+x)/2)-||y-x||²/(8η)].
This is equality of measures at every state, not merely ν-almost every state. The same S satisfies Λ.IsCondKernel(S), and both marginals of Λ equal ν.

There exists a surjective real-linear isometry e:N≃H such that i(e(u))=M(u) for every u. For that e there exists a real-linear isometry U:L→L satisfying, for every g in L, U(g)=g∘F J-almost everywhere; U(U(g))=g for every g; and U as a bounded endomorphism is selfadjoint. For these witnesses there exists a bounded real-linear T:N→N which is selfadjoint and, for every u in N, satisfies ||T(u)||≤||u||, T(u)(y)=∫u(x) S(y)(dx) for ν-almost every y, and ∫T(u)dν=∫u dν. The exceptional null set for the kernel-action identity may depend on u.

Define A:H→H as the orthogonal compression of U, A=proj_H∘U∘i, and B:H→L by B=(I-P)∘U∘P∘i. These are definitions; the subsequently asserted properties are A=e∘T∘e⁻¹, A selfadjoint, ||A(f)||≤||f|| for every f in H, and P(B(f))=0 for every f in H.

There exists a bounded endomorphism Γ of N which is positive, obeys Γ²=I-T², and commutes with T. Define ΓP=e∘Γ∘e⁻¹:H→H. Then ΓP is positive, ΓP²=I-A², ΓP commutes with A, and B*∘B=ΓP². Positivity has the supplied meaning selfadjoint with nonnegative quadratic form.

There exists q in N which is equal ν-almost everywhere to the constant 1, satisfies T(q)=q, and obeys <q,u>=∫u dν for every u in N. Define qP=e(q) and H0=HP0=ker(f↦<qP,f>) within H. Its inherited complete real Hilbert structures are local internal structures. Define γ=2sqrt(αη)/(1+αη). Then, for every f in H, f belongs to H0 exactly when ∫e⁻¹(f)dν=0. Also ΓP(qP)=0 and γ>0.

There exists a bounded Γ0=ΓP0:H0→H0 whose inclusion into H equals ΓP on H0. The SAME Γ0 is positive, Γ0-γI is positive, and Γ0 is a unit. There exists a bounded Inv:H0→H0 with Inv∘Γ0=Γ0∘Inv=I, ||Inv||≤1/γ, and Inv selfadjoint. There exists a bounded A0:H0→H0 which restricts A, is selfadjoint, commutes with Γ0, satisfies A0²+Γ0²=I, and commutes with that SAME Inv. These restricted objects and the inverse are concluded witnesses, not extra caller premises.

Define K=Hperp=ker(P) inside L, with internally inherited complete real Hilbert structures; K is the zero-conditional-expectation subspace, not just the globally zero-mean subspace. Let i0:H0→H and j:K→L be inclusions. There exists a bounded B0:H0→K with j∘B0=B∘i0. There exists a bounded V0:H0→K such that V0=B0∘Inv, B0=V0∘Γ0, V0*∘V0=I on H0, and ||V0(f)||=||f|| for every f in H0. No surjectivity of V0 onto K and no V0∘V0*=I on K is asserted.

There exists a bounded R:L→K satisfying j(R(g))=g-P(g) for every g in L and B*(g)=i0(B0*(R(g))) for EVERY g in L. Define D:K→K by D=R∘U∘j. Then j(D(h))=U(j(h))-P(U(j(h))) for every h in K, and V0*∘D=-(A0∘V0*) as operators from ALL of K to H0. This operator identity is not restricted to the range of V0.

For every f in L whose Bochner integral under J is zero, there exists fP in H0 with i0(fP)=CE(f). Define fperp=R(f) in K and fV=V0*(fperp) in H0. Then B*(j(fperp))=i0(Γ0(fV)), i0(Γ0(fV))=ΓP(i0(fV)), ||f||²=||fP||²+||fperp||², and ||fV||≤||fperp||.
For this f and these internally determined components define g=U(P(f)-(f-P(f))) in L. The output has zero J-integral. There exists gP in H0 with i0(gP)=CE(g). Define gperp=R(g) and gV=V0*(gperp). The proposition THEN ASSERTS gP=A0(fP)-Γ0(fV) and gV=Γ0(fP)+A0(fV), followed by ||gP||²+||gV||²=||fP||²+||fV||². These formulas are not the definitions of gP or gV; gP is tied to CE(g), and gV is independently defined by V0*R(g).
Finally, within this centered-input/output witness scope define C:H0×H0→ℝ by C(u,v)=(||u||²-||v||²)/2-<A0(Inv(u)),v>. Then
C(gP,gV)-C(fP,fV)=-||fP||²+||fV||²,
and for every u,v,r in H0,
C(u+Γ0(r),v-A0(r))-C(u,v)=<u,Inv(r)>+||r||²/2.
All existential witnesses above are chosen outside the final universal centered f; fP and gP are inside its implication. The final universal u,v,r is syntactically inside the chosen gP/C branch for each centered f. No unproved premise concerning these witnesses is added to the original conditions.

{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

    (hα : 0 < (α : ℝ)) (hαβ : α ≤ β) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E,
      (α : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (β : ℝ)*‖v‖^2)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hβη : (β : ℝ)*η ≤ 1) :
    let μ := (volume : Measure E).tilted (fun x => -V x)
    let J := (μ.prod (stdGaussian E)).map
      (fun p : E × E => (p.1,p.1+Real.sqrt η • p.2))
    let ν := J.snd
    let Λ := J.map (fun p : E × E => (p.2,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2))
    let F := fun p : E × E => (p.1,(2 : ℝ) • p.1-p.2)
    let mY := MeasurableSpace.comap Prod.snd (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E)
    letI : MeasurableSpace (E × E) := Prod.instMeasurableSpace
    letI : Fact (mY ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (E × E))) :=
      ⟨measurable_snd.comap_le⟩
    let HP := lpMeas ℝ ℝ mY 2 J
    let P : Lp ℝ 2 J →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J :=
      HP.subtypeL ∘L condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (μ := J) measurable_snd.comap_le
    let hp : MeasurePreserving (Prod.snd : E × E → E) J ν := ⟨measurable_snd,rfl⟩
    let M : Lp ℝ 2 ν →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J := Lp.compMeasurePreservingₗᵢ ℝ Prod.snd hp
    IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure J ∧ IsProbabilityMeasure ν ∧
    HP = P.toLinearMap.range ∧
    (∀ f : HP, P (f : Lp ℝ 2 J) = f) ∧
    ∃ S : Kernel E E, IsMarkovKernel S ∧
      (∀ y, S y = (volume : Measure E).tilted

      Λ.IsCondKernel S ∧ Λ.fst = ν ∧ Λ.snd = ν ∧
      ∃ e : Lp ℝ 2 ν ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] HP,

        ∃ U : Lp ℝ 2 J →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 J,

                letI : InnerProductSpace ℝ HP0 := HP0.innerProductSpace
                letI : CompleteSpace HP0 := (innerSL ℝ qP).isClosed_ker.completeSpace_coe
